rows.shows: The live numeral has a curved head and foot of 2 over an earlier straight stroke; the cancelled letter is multiply retraced. L has a looped base; ens lacks a point.
The final low horizontal group does not separate m/e/n enough to decide whether the ending is abbreviated.
A single high l-loop is followed by e and the low r-a run; the final a is visible. There is no point after the underlined name.
Rounded S and single-staff P; the cancelled beginning ends in the tall t of Soit. Two near-vertical ditto strokes stand at the next line, not an equals sign.
The ending of partie(s) runs off shallowly; a separately scribbled-out word remains above the following line, with only a possible une recoverable.
The f has full letter height and a deep descender. No detached point follows the final t of tot in this display (the earlier underlined tot. does have one).
The first subscript has a closed p-like head and descender, so cannot securely be 1. Final n is a single low arch; the second inequality glyph lacks an unambiguous cross stroke.
No plus appears before infinity. The clipped rightmost bracket has a vertical right stroke and feet turning left, supporting ] even though an open interval would be expected.
rows.consequential: The rightmost interval is transcribed with the visible closing ] and no added plus before infinity; the mathematical expectation is not substituted for the ink.
